items.title: Kavach v4.0 loco orders - ₹3,353 cr in hand for FY27 delivery
items.text: HBL holds Letters of Acceptance from CLW (₹1,714 cr), BLW (₹800 cr + ₹180 cr), ICF Chennai (₹575 cr), and PLW (₹83.81 cr), all for v4.0 on-board Kavach equipment to be completed within 12 months. These orders alone exceed the ₹1,000 cr loco revenue management targets for FY27, locking in near-term earnings visibility from the company's largest growth segment.

items.title: Kavach trackside and station rollout - ₹900 cr invoicing target for FY27
items.text: HBL and its consortium partner hold Letters of Acceptance from Western Railway (48 stations, 428 km), Central Railway (413 stations, 3,900 km), and North Central Railway, with management planning ₹900 cr of station revenue in FY27 and a further ₹400 cr in FY28. This adds a second large Kavach revenue stream that extends the order book runway into FY28.

items.title: Kavach v4.0 first-mover certification
items.text: HBL was the first OEM to obtain v4.0 certification on 13 May 2025 and the first to demonstrate the system against the frozen specification on 24 September 2024, with tenders for 19,000 km floated and 16,000 km already contracted under v4.0. Being the only certified v4.0 supplier at the start of the national rollout positions HBL to capture a disproportionate share of the initial wave of orders.

items.title: Electric drive trucks - assembly start October 2026
items.text: HBL will assemble 35-ton and 55-ton GVW electric trucks using bought-out components and in-house lithium-ion batteries, with sales now scheduled to begin in October 2026 after a one-year delay to resolve magnet and design issues. The asset-light assembly model requires minimal capex and targets higher-margin niche users, creating a new revenue vertical adjacent to the company's existing battery and power-electronics capabilities.

items.title: Lithium-ion battery - Siemens global sourcing win and defence contracts
items.text: Siemens Germany selected HBL as one of two global sources for lithium-ion batteries for Siemens-built trains and metro cars, and defence customers abroad are already purchasing HBL batteries for armoured vehicles. These customised, engineering-intensive orders carry higher margins than standard telecom batteries and validate HBL's shift toward specialised lithium-ion applications.

items.title: Lithium-ion cell capex - ₹100 cr plant for in-house high-energy-density cells
items.text: HBL is implementing a capex plan of about ₹100 cr in FY25 to make high-energy-density lithium-ion cells in-house, building on a ₹40 cr pilot plant completed two years earlier. Bringing cell production in-house secures supply and improves margins for the company's own e-truck batteries and for the Siemens and defence lithium-ion programmes.

items.title: Green Maritime Propulsion JV with Cochin Shipyard
items.text: HBL (60%) and Cochin Shipyard (40%) signed a joint venture agreement on 25 March 2026 to develop electric mobility and energy storage solutions for maritime applications, with an initial capital of ₹9 cr. The partnership pairs HBL's battery and power-electronics technology with India's largest shipbuilder, opening a new addressable market in vessel electrification.

items.title: Defence electronics - electronic fuzes as largest defence revenue driver
items.text: HBL is the only company in India with 100% indigenised electronic fuzes for grenades, artillery shells, rockets, missiles, and air-dropped bombs, and management states this will be the largest single contributor to defence segment revenues. A sole-supplier position in a consumable munitions component creates a recurring, high-barrier revenue stream as defence orders scale.

items.title: Industrial battery exports - 40% growth with strong FY26 order book
items.text: Exports of industrial lead-acid and nickel-cadmium batteries grew 40% in FY25, driven by new OEM and EPC customers particularly in the Middle East, and the order book as of 31 March 2025 for FY26 supplies is described as very strong. Capacity for export-focused nickel-cadmium pocket-plate batteries has already been enhanced through line balancing, allowing the company to convert a strong pipeline without additional major capex.
